storing-memories-amnesia.alt: A timeline with a brain injury or illness marked in the middle. An orange arrow points back in time from the injury: retrograde amnesia, where memories from before the injury are lost, for example a person who cannot recall the weeks before a car crash. A blue arrow points forward in time from the injury: anterograde amnesia, where new long-term memories cannot be formed after it, for example a person who can chat for a minute but cannot remember the talk an hour later. A note says that in anterograde amnesia, skills (procedural memory) can often still be learned.
